_readme: Suno makes the song in every song ad (the owner, 2026-10-28: "for all song ads, we're just using Suno. It's the best."). It has no API: the song-ad chain writes the boxes from this sheet (tools/video-production/machine/song.py --suno) and a person or a browser session types them into suno.com; the take comes back through the song gate (song.py --from-file).
Registry id `suno` (components/models, transport manual); the Generative Model House's sound.song names it.
No brand, product, person or format word appears in this file.
Draft: every entry is status draft until the owner approves it.
label: Suno (v5 / v5.5, by hand, no API)

vendor_ids.door: manual: typed into suno.com from song/suno-inputs.json; the Model House job sound.song
vendor_ids.versions: v6 seen in the app on 2026-10-28 (the newest; limits above were tested on v5 / v5.5 and are unconfirmed on v6); v5, v5.5, v4.5 still selectable

limits.style_box_chars: about 1,000 on v5 / v5.5 (community-tested; Suno publishes no limits table); older v4 about 200; text past the limit is cut silently
limits.lyrics_box_chars: sources conflict: about 3,000 or up to 5,000; stay near 2,500
limits.style_descriptors: 3 to 5 simple, 8 to 15 detailed, about 20 maximum; sweet spot 4 to 7
limits.custom_models: 6 tracks minimum, 3 per account (Pro or Premier)
limits.numbers_are: community figures except the sliders, which are Suno's own help page; confirm in the app before a batch

house.how: the chain writes style, exclude, lyrics (a section tag over every part) and sliders from the brief's song block and its style row's `suno` line; the take goes through the same song gate as any song ad (words heard in order, last line finished)
house.door: manual (registry transport), by hand on suno.com

inputs.name: style of music
inputs.what: The sound of the song: genre, tempo, mood, instruments, vocal, era.
inputs.allowed: comma-separated tags, about 1,000 characters; earlier tags weigh more
inputs.we_send: genre + BPM + mood + 2-3 instruments + vocal + era, 4 to 7 descriptors, front-loaded

inputs.name: lyrics
inputs.what: The words sung, with section tags.
inputs.allowed: text with [Verse] [Chorus] style tags; never empty
inputs.we_send: the brief's song lines word for word, 6 to 10 syllables a line, 4 lines a section

inputs.name: exclude styles
inputs.allowed: short list; more reliable than 'no X' in the style box; do not overload

inputs.name: weirdness
inputs.what: Safe to chaotic; 50 is the normal result.
inputs.we_send: 20 to 30 for a song ad (commercial, safe)

inputs.name: style influence
inputs.what: How strictly the style box is followed.
inputs.we_send: 70 to 90 for vague tags, 40 to 60 for specific ones

inputs.name: audio influence
inputs.what: How much an uploaded audio steers the result (appears with an upload).
inputs.we_send: only when a reference is uploaded

inputs.name: instrumental
inputs.allowed: toggle, or [Instrumental] in the style box

inputs.name: model version
inputs.we_send: v5 for steadiness; v5.5 is more expressive but can drift to generic pop mid-track

inputs.name: Voices / Personas
inputs.allowed: upload 15 s to 4 min (best 2 min kept); paid tier
inputs.we_send: not used unless a voice is ruled for the brand

inputs.name: Extend / Cover
inputs.what: Lengthen a song or re-sing it on another model.
inputs.we_send: generate on v5, then Cover on v5.5 if more expression is wanted

inputs.name: structure tags
inputs.what: Section labels: Intro, Verse, Pre-Chorus, Chorus, Bridge, Break, Solo, Build, Outro, End.
inputs.allowed: in the lyrics box; [Instrumental Break] is more reliable than [Bridge]
inputs.we_send: one per section; Bridge and Outro once each

inputs.name: vocal tags
inputs.allowed: either box; a mid-song change goes in the lyrics just before that section
inputs.we_send: style box for the main vocal, lyrics for a change

inputs.name: BPM
inputs.allowed: number, always with a mood word

structure.rule: Style box order: genre, tempo, mood, instruments, vocal style, era, reference. Put what matters most first.
Use 4 to 7 descriptors; cut any two that say the same thing; stacking 15 or more dilutes it.
One primary genre plus one modifier, three at most; strong genres (pop, rock, electronic) override weak ones (grunge, math rock, swing).
Name specific instruments, two or three core textures only.
Give BPM as a number and always pair it with a mood word.
Put a section tag over every part of the lyrics; without them the whole song sits at one energy.
Set the main vocal in the style box and the gender explicitly; use the lyrics box for a change within the song.
Use the Exclude field for unwanted traits rather than 'no X' in the style box, and keep it to two or three.
Move one slider at a time; weirdness low for commercial work; style influence high when the tags are vague.
Write 6 to 10 syllable lines and 4-line sections; shorter lyrics make shorter songs, use Extend for length.
When a take misses, change one thing before regenerating; the same prompt again gives the same result.
Whatever Suno makes goes through the same song gate as any song ad: every script line heard in order, last line finished. Suno may sing words the lyrics do not hold.
structure.ours: song gate on the downloaded file

avoid.text: Short poetic lines, ALL CAPS phrases or quotes in the style box: they get sung.
'Don't' or 'no X' phrasing inside the style box.
Contradictory tags such as calm with aggressive, or more than three genres.
A BPM with no mood word.
Putting the vocal style only in the lyrics box.
More than three or four instruments.
Relying on 'ethereal', 'crescendo' or 'realistic', and on chorus modifiers: they are often ignored or overridden.
More than about seven elements in one pipe-stacked tag, or Bridge/Outro/Build used more than once.
Trusting v5.5 to hold the style the whole way: it can drift to generic pop or change when extended.
Naming a living artist as the style: the song-ad style is a ruled row, no free text.
